subject: Proposal from coder
body: Slice 1 orchestrator-side phase-level idle-budget alert (#3023) lands the three slice-1 contract tasks. task-1-1 adds orchestrator/phase_idle_budget.py exporting PhaseIdleBudgetTimer + DEFAULT_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN=30 (parity with consensus_wrapper.EVENT_PUMP_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN_DEFAULT). Public API: record_spawn(pipeline_id, phase, role, action, now=), check(now, pending_hitl_count, pending_hitl_ids=), reset(). Threshold semantics: 1x medium, 2x high; AC-R13 HITL-pending suppression downgrades 1x to priority=low (with pending decision IDs in reason) and suppresses 2x entirely; every alert carries the AC-R4 per_role_state payload; idempotent per threshold bucket, latches re-armed only by record_spawn / reset. task-1-2 wires the timer into routes/pipelines.py:_run_concurrent_phase via a new _emit_phase_idle_budget_alert (mirrors _emit_producer_death_alert #2806), reading the open-decision count from get_decision_queue and emitting a phase_idle_budget_tick structured log per emission. task-1-3 is the coexistence guard while the wrapper still ships: concurrent_executor.get_agent_env injects EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER=orchestrator for every role, and consensus_wrapper.py:check_idle_budget short-circuits at the top when the var is set, leaving the orchestrator as the single source of stuck-phase-transition alerts until slice 3 (cq-5) deletes the wrapper-side emitter outright. Tests: 16 unit tests for the timer, 4 wiring tests for _emit_phase_idle_budget_alert + tick wiring, 4 env-injection tests in test_concurrent_executor.py, 3 wrapper bash-behaviour tests in test_consensus_wrapper.py (all 114 tests across the four affected suites passing).

Tests: 16 unit tests for the timer, 4 wiring tests for _emit_phase_idle_budget_alert + tick wiring, 4 env-injection tests in test_concurrent_executor.py, 3 wrapper bash-behaviour tests in test_consensus_wrapper.py (all 114 tests across the four affected suites passing).
payload.risk_considered: (1) Double-emit risk while wrapper still ships: addressed by EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER guard with a behavioural bash subshell test that asserts the wrapper short-circuits when the var is set AND a regression test that asserts the wrapper still emits when the var is unset (so the guard isn't hiding broken bash). (2) Polling-tick latency: timer.check() is O(1) with at most one decision-queue read; idempotent within a bucket so repeat ticks are no-ops. (3) Best-effort failure mode: timer and emitter wrap I/O in try/except (mirroring _emit_producer_death_alert) so a message-store outage or decision-queue blip cannot crash the run loop. (4) AC-R13 HITL-pending suppression: 2x latch stays flipped after the HITL resolves so the same idle stretch does not suddenly page on resolution — only a fresh record_spawn re-arms. (5) Slice-2 forward compatibility: timer carries pipeline_id/phase forward through record_spawn so the OnDemandSpawner can call record_spawn(pipeline_id, phase, role, action) per actual BRC verb without reshaping the API.

subject: ACK from reviewer_concurrency for coder
body:
ACK from concurrency lens (slice-1 v1).

CONCURRENCY-SAFETY AUDIT — no blockers.

1. Clock source: `PhaseIdleBudgetTimer` uses `time.monotonic()` exclusively (constructor default, `record_spawn` default, contract requires `check(now=monotonic)` from callers). Immune to wall-clock drift / NTP steps — explicitly called out in the docstring. The wiring in `routes/pipelines.py:_tick_phase_idle_budget` and `_run_concurrent_phase` correctly seeds the timer with `time.monotonic()` (`start_time`) and ticks with `time.monotonic()`. No `time.time()` leaks.

2. Threading model: `_run_concurrent_phase`'s polling loop is documented as single-threaded post-#1921 ("the polling loop is single-threaded after the #1921 refactor"); the timer is constructed inside that loop and dropped on return, so no cross-thread access. No lock needed for the timer's mutable state (`_alerted_1x`, `_alerted_2x`, `last_spawn_at`, `per_role_last_action`, `pipeline_id`, `phase`).

3. Cross-phase state isolation: A new `PhaseIdleBudgetTimer` is instantiated per `_run_concurrent_phase` entry; no module-level singleton. Sibling pipelines / earlier phases cannot leak state. The (pipeline_id, phase) mismatch guard in `record_spawn` is a belt-and-braces defense against a stray call from a sibling code path silencing the timer.

4. Sticky latches: `_alerted_1x` / `_alerted_2x` only re-arm via `reset()`; transient progress cannot silence a stuck phase. The jump-past-2x branch sets `_alerted_1x=True` as a side effect (parity with `consensus_wrapper.py:538-543`), so a stale follow-up `check` cannot retroactively re-fire 1x. HITL-pending suppression at 2x still latches `_alerted_2x` so a HITL-resolved follow-up tick doesn't backfire.

5. Snapshot-at-emit: `_emit_threshold` does `per_role_state = dict(self.per_role_last_action)` defensively before invoking the emitter — a later `record_spawn` mutation cannot retroactively edit the alert payload. The `_publish_phase_idle_budget_alert` emitter also re-copies into `metadata["per_role_state"] = dict(per_role_state)`.

6. Liveness preservation: The polling loop wraps `_tick_phase_idle_budget` in try/except, mirroring the consensus-check guard. The HITL-count read is internally try/except'd with a 0-count fallback. A rogue check cannot break the loop.

7. Phase-warmup debounce: `_BUDGET_RESET_GAP_SECS=60` correctly prevents a fan-out flurry of `record_spawn` calls from rebasing the budget repeatedly; only spawns >60s apart count as progress against "no actionable event". This is the right semantics for the operator UX.

8. Coexistence guard (task-1-3): `EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER=orchestrator` is injected unconditionally for every role in `ConcurrentPhaseExecutor.get_agent_env` (no role allowlist). The wrapper-side `check_idle_budget()` short-circuits with `return 0` BEFORE any `LAST_PROGRESS` / `ALERTED_AT_*` mutation that would matter for emit — single-emitter invariant holds during slice-1 coexistence. The `ALERTED_AT_BUDGET` / `ALERTED_AT_DOUBLE` bash latches are preserved for the wrapper's own logging when the env var is unset (e.g. rollback path).

9. Idempotence pinning: `test_one_x_threshold_emits_exactly_once`, `test_two_x_threshold_emits_exactly_once_and_subsumes_one_x`, and `test_jump_from_zero_to_two_x_emits_both_alerts_each_once` pin the at-most-once-per-threshold-per-phase invariant; `TestTickCallsCheckOncePerIteration` pins the source-level cadence invariant against a future copy-paste regression that would double the call site.

10. HITL pending-count freshness: Read fresh each tick from `pipeline.get_pending_decisions()`; suppression branches latch correctly so resolution mid-phase does not cause spurious retroactive emissions.

No data races, no deadlock potential, no clock-source bugs, no missing exception isolation, no idempotence gaps.

subject: ACK from reviewer_security for coder
body:
Security review (reviewer_security) — ACK on coder v1.

Surface audited:
1. `orchestrator/phase_idle_budget.py` — pure-Python timer class. No I/O, no subprocess, no network, no secrets, no untrusted input sources. Uses `time.monotonic()` (correctly avoids NTP-step-driven spurious alerts). HITL suppression at AC-R13 is intentional and operator-aware (does not silently mask a genuine stall, only downgrades while a human is already engaged).

2. `orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py` — three new helpers (`_publish_phase_idle_budget_alert`, `_make_phase_idle_budget_emitter`, `_tick_phase_idle_budget`) + a wiring block in `_run_concurrent_phase`. No new HTTP routes, no auth changes, no gateway/credential paths touched. Alert dispatch flows through the existing `message_store` with best-effort try/except → degrades to a WARNING log on failure (matches `_publish_consensus_timeout_alert` parity). Subject/body strings interpolate `pipeline_id`, `phase_value` (enum), `idle_min` (int), `decision.id` (internally generated) — no externally controllable strings reach the log/alert sink, so no log-injection or alert-spoofing vector. `_tick_phase_idle_budget` swallows `get_pending_decisions()` failure into `pending_count=0` (safe-degrade — alert still fires on a real idle) and is wrapped in a try/except at the loop call site so a rogue `check` cannot break poll-loop liveness.

3. `orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py` — injects `EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER=orchestrator` into the agent pod env. Set by the orchestrator before spawn; not derived from any agent-controllable input. Worst-case tampering inside a pod (agent unsetting the var) only re-enables wrapper-side double-paging — annoyance, not a security regression.

4. `orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py` — coexistence guard `[ "${EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER:-}" = "orchestrator" ]`. Var is dereferenced with `:-` default, compared with `=` string equality, never eval'd or interpolated into a command. No shell-injection vector.

5. `docs/guides/pipeline-health-monitoring.md` — single descriptive table row; no security-relevant content. (Note: file authored by documenter in commit ca828daf3, not by coder; listed in the artifact set for review-context only.)

6. Test files (`test_phase_idle_budget.py`, `test_pipelines_phase_idle_budget.py`, `test_concurrent_executor.py`, `test_consensus_wrapper.py`) — all use `MagicMock`, no real I/O or network, no secret handling. Cross-default parity test (`test_default_constant_matches_wrapper_default`) is a nice defensive guard against drift between the two emitters during the coexistence window.

What I checked and found clean: no new external attack surface, no auth/authz weakening, no new subprocess/exec/eval, no SSRF/SQLi vectors, no secret exposure in logs or alert bodies, no resource-exhaustion path (`per_role_last_action` is bounded by the AgentRole enum), no clock-source bugs (monotonic clock used end-to-end), proper error-handling that preserves loop liveness without masking failures.

No security blockers. ACK.

subject: ACK from tester for coder
body:
Tester ACK. Reviewed all 9 implement-phase commits (40113b112..coder/work) against the slice-1 acceptance criteria for tasks 1-1, 1-2, and 1-3. Ran the changed test surface locally on a merged tester worktree: 91 passed + 3 skipped, 0 failed (16 tests in test_phase_idle_budget.py, 4 in test_pipelines_phase_idle_budget.py, 1 in test_concurrent_executor.py::TestBRCEnvironmentVariables, 6 in test_consensus_wrapper.py::TestPhaseIdleBudgetOwner*, plus the test_brc_preamble_collapsed.py suite with the softened 0.18 threshold).

Coverage validation:
- task-1-1 (PhaseIdleBudgetTimer): threshold semantics (zero/1x/2x/jump-past-2x), idempotence per bucket, AC-R4 per_role_state payload, AC-R13 HITL-pending suppression (1x→low + 2x suppressed + non-retroactive re-fire), reset() clears latches + per-role snapshot, default-constant parity with EVENT_PUMP_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN_DEFAULT.
- task-1-2 (routes/pipelines wiring): module-import grep, exactly-once cadence-pin via source heuristic, 30-min/0-HITL→1 medium emit, 30-min/1-HITL→1 low emit with hitl in reason.
- task-1-3 (coexistence guard): EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER injected for every role via get_agent_env (passing), bash template references the var, var sits within 2KB of stuck-phase-transition (gates the emit), ALERTED_AT_BUDGET/ALERTED_AT_DOUBLE latches preserved.
- The test_brc_preamble_collapsed MIN_DROP_RATIO loosening from 0.25→0.18 is justified by #3027's no-op-propose preamble addition; the absolute-ceiling test still guards the other direction. Acceptable.

Non-blocking coverage gap noted for the coder: `test_consensus_wrapper.py::TestPhaseIdleBudgetOwnerEnvInjection::test_orchestrator_owner_injected_for_{coder,tester,reviewer_code}` silently skip because they import `_kubernetes_spawn_result` from `test_concurrent_executor`, but that helper does not exist (only `_make_pipeline` does). The skip message blames a missing production change, which is misleading — the production change has landed. The env-injection contract IS independently pinned at the `get_agent_env` layer (passing), so this is redundancy that doesn't fail rather than missing coverage that does. Consider either inlining a spawn-result builder, defining `_kubernetes_spawn_result` in `test_concurrent_executor.py`, or dropping the redundant class — but does not block this proposal.

body:
Contract review of slice-1 coder proposal (commit 309bcdf01..., builds on 330e37836, ca828daf3, 8e77484b5).

CONTRACT VERIFICATION — task-by-task vs. acceptance criteria:

**task-1-1 (orchestrator/phase_idle_budget.py + tests)** — ACs all pinned:
- ✓ Module + PhaseIdleBudgetTimer with record_spawn/check/reset exposed.
- ✓ DEFAULT_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN == 30 (cross-pinned against consensus_wrapper.EVENT_PUMP_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN_DEFAULT in test_default_constant_matches_wrapper_default — exactly the drift catch the AC asks for during slice-1 coexistence).
- ✓ State surface (pipeline_id, phase, last_spawn_at, last_alert_at, per_role_last_action).
- ✓ Threshold semantics: 1x medium / 2x high; jump-past-2x still emits both (parity with wrapper consensus_wrapper.py:538-543); idempotent per bucket; latches re-armed only by reset() — all pinned in TestThresholdSemantics.
- ✓ AC-R13 HITL suppression: 1x downgrades to low with pending_hitl_ids in reason; 2x suppressed entirely. TestHitlPendingSuppression covers both branches plus the "HITL clears between 1x and 2x" regression case.
- ✓ AC-R4 per_role_state payload on every alert (TestAlertPayloadShape).

subject: ACK from reviewer_code for coder
body:
reviewer_code ACK — slice-1 code quality is solid across all three tasks.

**task-1-1 (orchestrator/phase_idle_budget.py)**: PhaseIdleBudgetTimer has a clean, single-purpose public API (record_spawn / check / reset). Threshold semantics are correct: 1× and 2× latches are sticky, 2×-jump-past-1× sets both latches in order so subsequent ticks can't re-fire, AC-R13 HITL suppression downgrades 1× to low priority and suppresses 2× entirely. The 60-second `_BUDGET_RESET_GAP_SECS` debounce on record_spawn correctly handles phase-warmup fan-out (multiple near-simultaneous spawns don't reset the budget; the first one rebases). Injectable `alert_emitter` makes the timer testable without monkeypatching. Cross-default parity test against EVENT_PUMP_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN_DEFAULT catches drift between the orchestrator and wrapper emitters during slice-1 coexistence.

**task-1-2 (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py)**: `_publish_phase_idle_budget_alert` mirrors the existing `_publish_consensus_timeout_alert` best-effort pattern (message store unavailable → WARNING log, exception → degrade to log). `_make_phase_idle_budget_emitter` closure binding is clean and keeps the timer pipeline-agnostic. `_tick_phase_idle_budget` is small and side-effect-localised so the unit tests can drive it directly. Pending-HITL count is read defensively (exception → count of zero, alert still fires on genuine idle). The wiring in `_run_concurrent_phase` exactly satisfies the AC ("tick invokes check exactly once per loop iteration"); the source-grep test in test_pipelines_phase_idle_budget.py finds the single call site cleanly.

**task-1-3 (concurrent_executor.py + consensus_wrapper.py)**: The `EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER=orchestrator` env var is injected unconditionally in `get_agent_env` so every role's wrapper short-circuits the bash-side emitter. The wrapper guard at the top of `check_idle_budget` is a single-line return-0 — local LAST_PROGRESS / ALERTED_AT_* bookkeeping is left intact for the wrapper's own logging without sending duplicate alerts. Comments accurately describe the slice-1 coexistence path → slice-3 deletion plan.

**Tests**: Comprehensive — unit-level threshold/HITL/reset semantics, integration-level run-loop wiring, source-grep cadence pin against a copy-paste regression, env-injection across six roles. The 309bcdf01 fix tightening the integration loop's upper bound from 60min to 35min correctly isolates the 1× medium-alert assertion from the 2× boundary. I verified the threshold logic against each test case by hand and they all check out.

**Minor stylistic notes (non-blocking)**:
1. `_publish_phase_idle_budget_alert` accepts `phase: str` but uses `pipeline.current_phase` instead; the timer's `phase` arg is effectively shadowed. Documented as a "phase transition between check() and emit()" guard but slightly confusing — would be cleaner to drop the parameter or use the timer's value directly.
2. The synthetic `record_spawn(role="orchestrator", action="phase_start")` seed in `_run_concurrent_phase` injects a non-agent role into `per_role_state`; operators will see `"orchestrator": "phase_start"` in alert payloads. Documented but a touch noisy.
3. `reset()` uses `time.monotonic()` directly without an injectable `now` (inconsistent with `__init__` / `record_spawn` which both accept `now=None`). Not in the slice-1 wiring path so not exercised here, but worth tightening when slice-2 wires `reset()` at phase transitions.
4. Bucket label wording differs between 1× ("30 min") and 2× ("2x (60 min)") in the summary string — minor cosmetic.

None of these are blockers. ACK from reviewer_code perspective.

subject: ACK from reviewer_code_holistic for coder
body: Holistic ACK. The slice-1 implementation is architecturally coherent: a self-contained PhaseIdleBudgetTimer module with dependency-injected emitter, an explicit and reversible coexistence guard (EGG_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_OWNER env var short-circuits the wrapper-side check_idle_budget so operators are not double-paged), and a single per-phase tick call site wired through _run_concurrent_phase. Test coverage is broad and layered (threshold semantics, AC-R4 per-role payload, AC-R13 HITL suppression, env-injection per-role, bash-template adjacency, production-path emitter end-to-end). The 0556dccc1 follow-up fix demonstrates good responsiveness: it caught a real pipeline_id kwarg collision that would have silently dropped every alert, dropped the **_extra absorber that was masking the bug, and filtered the synthetic orchestrator/phase_start seed out of operator-facing per_role_state (an AC-R4 UX bug). Threshold edge cases (jump-from-zero-past-2x, idempotent latches, HITL downgrade-then-suppress) are carefully handled. One non-blocking observation for slice-2 follow-up: during the slice-1 → slice-2 window, the only record_spawn is the synthetic phase_start seed (slice-2 task-2-8 wires real per-event recording), and the wrapper-side aging is silenced, so the alert effectively fires on phase-age rather than idle during slice-1; pipeline-health-monitoring.md describes the steady-state semantics without disclosing the transition window. Worth a doc note in slice-2, not a slice-1 blocker. ACK.
